failure_summary.description: The answer selected an embedded place or list item instead of the entity requested by the clue's sentence structure.
The answer was semantically related but at the wrong granularity, such as an expanded name or title, an unnecessary qualifier, or a country where an adjective was requested.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers parsing the answer slot and using the requested part of speech, so repeating those rules would not address the two slot-selection errors. The more common pattern is over-expanding or over-specifying an otherwise identified answer. Replacing the name-form instruction with a concrete minimality check makes the existing shortest-answer principle easier to apply.

edits.target: - Use the context-supported conventional form of a name or answer, and include additional name parts only when needed to distinguish otherwise-confusable entities.
edits.content: - Use the context-supported conventional form of a name or answer, and include additional name parts or modifiers only when the clue requires them or they distinguish otherwise-confusable entities. As a final exact-match check, remove any unnecessary given name, organization suffix, subtitle, or descriptive qualifier; if the shorter canonical form still uniquely fills the requested slot, return that form. Do not expand a conventional short name or title into a longer official form solely because the context displays it.
